newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian govt funds A$10 mln steel city aid plan.
newsitem.headline: Australian govt funds A$10 mln steel city aid plan.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday the government would provide A$10 million to help the city of Newcastle recover from the planned closure of its steel plant.
Howard, who visited the east coast city on Wednesday, said the package would finance projects that would "generate longer term economic and employment opportunities in the region".
The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, Australia's largest company, is due to end steelmaking in the city, north of Sydney, in 1999.

The funding was made in cooperation with the New South Wales (NSW) state government and BHP, Howard said, adding that it was in addition to national government environment and tourist development funding.
The NSW government announced its own A$10 million assistance package for the city earlier this year, with the national government pledging to match the move.
"In the Commonwealth's view, these funds should be pooled and allocated if possible to one major project with long term economic potential," Howard said in a statement.
"While the changes to BHP steelworks will not take place for some time, these changes have caused uncertainty and anxiety which must be addressed sooner rather than later.
"Employees and local businesses can then plan with greater certainty and confidence for the future."
While in Newcastle, Howard has been talking with union and community leaders, BHP officials and touring the steel plant.
